definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the complex universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(C)

inputs.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. Its endomorphisms x,y,h satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y and xy−yx=h. The vector v∈V is nonzero and satisfies xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an arbitrary free abelian subgroup with an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and M is stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! (r∈N). The induced x,y,h actions on V(K)=M⊗_Z K are the actions in the target.
Let K be any field, M any Z-module, and b a Z-basis of M indexed by an arbitrary type ι. There exists a K-basis B of K⊗_Z M indexed by the same ι with B_i=1⊗b_i.

argument.text: H001 identifies λ with its natural value and gives n=λ+1>0. Let ι=Fin n. By H003 an integer basis of M is also a complex basis of V. H002 says V has finite complex dimension λ+1=n. Therefore the index set of that supplied basis is finite with exactly n elements, and it can be relabelled by ι. This is the defining basis-cardinality characterization of finite dimension: any complex basis of an n-dimensional complex space has n elements. Thus there exists an integer basis of M indexed by ι which is a complex basis of V.

produces.statement: There exists an integer basis of M indexed by ι=Fin n, also a complex basis of V, and n=λ+1>0.

argument.text: Choose such a basis b using F001 and H003. Its integer span is all of M and its integer coordinates are unique. The identity of this choice is private to this proof; only its scalar extension and cardinality will be used.

produces.statement: b is an integer basis of M indexed by ι=Fin n.

argument.text: Apply M002 to the base ring Z, canonical Z-algebra K and the integer basis b from F002, obtaining the K-basis B of K⊗_Z M with B_i=1⊗b_i. Apply M007 to obtain σ. It is K-linear: for all m∈M,a,d∈K, σ(d·(m⊗a))=da⊗m=d·σ(m⊗a), and pure tensors span. The same calculation applies to the inverse. Thus σ is a K-linear equivalence for the K-action in D008.

produces.statement: B is a K-basis of K⊗_Z M indexed by ι, and σ:U→K⊗_Z M is a K-linear equivalence sending m⊗a to a⊗m.

argument.text: Define bK_i=σ^(-1)(B_i)=b_i⊗1. F003 implies this is a K-basis of U: apply σ to finite linear relations for independence, and pull back expansions in B for spanning. Apply M006 to field K, vector space U, index type ι and basis bK. It gives dim_K U=Nat.card ι=n=λ+1. This finite basis also proves finite dimensionality. Since n>0 by F001, the index 0 exists and its basis vector bK_0 is nonzero, so U≠0. This proves both clauses of the output statement; the conclusion is independent of the chosen b.

background_notes.fact: If V is a finite-dimensional complex vector space of dimension n and an integer basis of M has images forming a complex basis of V, then this common basis has a finite index set of cardinal n and can be reindexed by Fin n, preserving both basis properties.

grounds.reason: H002 gives the finite complex dimension λ+1.
H003 supplies an integer basis whose images form a complex basis.
H001 gives λ≥0, so D001 identifies the natural n with λ+1.

background_notes.justification: Take a complex basis with n elements, as furnished by finite dimension. The finite exchange argument bounds any finite independent family by the size of a finite spanning family: successively insert independent vectors into the spanning list and remove a vector with a nonzero coefficient, retaining spanning and the vectors previously inserted. Thus the supplied basis cannot have n+1 distinct indices and its index set is finite. If its size is k, applying the same bound in both directions to the two bases gives k≤n and n≤k, hence k=n. A bijection Fin n to its index set reindexes both the integer and complex families; bijections preserve finite relations and spanning expansions.

background_notes.fact: Every element of either balanced integer tensor product M⊗_Z K or K⊗_Z M is a finite sum of pure tensors. For the K-actions used here, the additive flip σ(m⊗a)=a⊗m is therefore K-linear, and its inverse is K-linear.

grounds.reason: D008 specifies U=M⊗_Z K and d·(m⊗a)=m⊗da.
H003 supplies the integer module M.
H001 supplies the field K and its integer-module structure.
M002 supplies the scalar-extended K-module and its basis on K⊗_Z M.
M007 supplies the additive flip equivalence and its pure-tensor formula.

background_notes.justification: The balanced tensor product is the additive group generated by pure tensors subject to the additive and balancing relations; negative generators can be absorbed into a tensor factor. Consequently each element is a finite sum of pure tensors. On such a tensor σ(d·(m⊗a))=(da)⊗m=d·σ(m⊗a), and additivity and distribution extend this equality to finite sums. For w in the target, σ(d·σ⁻¹(w))=dw=σ(σ⁻¹(dw)); injectivity gives d·σ⁻¹(w)=σ⁻¹(dw). Thus the inverse is also K-linear.
